title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For The Cash As Apple Leaves?
summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) throws off free cash worth 5.2% of its market value each year, against 4.4% for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median means one of two things: a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Here it is mostly the second: the cash comes from smartphone chips, and Apple is leaving.

title: Is Micron Stock Cheap, Or Are Its Profits Borrowed?
summary: Micron Technology (MU) ranks first in its peer group on revenue growth, operating margin and twelve-month stock return. It still trades at 20.7 times earnings, below a peer's 26.6. The gap is not an oversight. The market is paying Micron for what it earns now and refusing to pay for what it earns next.

title: How Far Can NVIDIA Stock Fall In A Demand Scare?
summary: NVIDIA (NVDA) stock trades near $212, about 10% below its 52-week high, and it has gone nowhere over the past three months. The company itself has not been standing still. So it is worth asking the uncomfortable question: how far does a stock like this fall when a real shock arrives, and how long would you wait to get it back.

title: Should You Buy Intel Stock For The Chips It Cannot Yet Make Enough Of?
summary: Intel (INTC) stock has returned about 295% over the past year, but it has given back 22% over the past three months. It trades roughly 31% below its 52-week high. The question now is what powers the next leg, and the answer is what Intel can build, not what it can sell.
